summary: Repeats CHOP channels before and after their original interval and can blend cycle seams to make animation or audio loops smoother.

key_params.name: before
key_params.note: Number of cycles before the original input

key_params.name: after
key_params.note: Number of cycles after the original input

key_params.name: extremes
key_params.note: Blend the end of the CHOP into the start

key_params.name: blendmethod
key_params.note: Preserve length, overlap, or insert blend region

key_params.name: blendfunc
key_params.note: Blend shape such as linear, ease, cubic, add, or hold

key_params.name: step
key_params.note: Shift next cycle to begin where prior cycle ended

key_concepts: Repeats input CHOP channels before and after their original interval, with fractional Cycles Before and Cycles After supported.
Mirror Cycles reverses every other generated cycle while leaving the first cycle unmirrored.
Blend Start to End can smooth the loop boundary; the official smooth-forever case depends on zero before/after cycles, a nonzero blend region, and Cycle extend conditions.
Blend Method changes the timing topology between preserving length, overlapping cycles, or inserting a blend region.
Blend Shape selects the interpolation or audio-oriented Add behavior used across the blended region.
Step and Step Scope offset selected channels so a later cycle begins where the previous cycle ended, which is useful for root-motion walk cycles.
common_gotchas: Cycle CHOP does not magically make bad endpoints loop; use blend region, extremes, or source cleanup for visible seams.
Blend Start to End is useful with Cycle extend conditions when before/after are zero and a nonzero region is set.
The Add blend shape is useful for looping audio but can increase amplitude.
Step should usually be scoped to root-motion channels, not every animated channel.
Fractional cycle counts can change output interval expectations for downstream CHOPs.
